page: Microsoft Azure F2als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 x86_64 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, providing 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with 1 thread per core. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, along with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. Memory is provisioned at 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no local storage and does not feature GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread processing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 3791.79 in the top 10% tier. Compression benchmarks reinforce this single-core efficiency, yielding 40.64 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 18.06 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, both ranking in the top tier. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics reflect the limitations of the dual-core footprint: multi-core stress-ng reaches an average 7556.2, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression yields 36.19 GB/sec in the bottom 25% tier. In instruction-specific testing, the PassMark CPU score is 6933.36 with an extended instructions rating of 5876.52 and an encryption score of 3188.37.

Memory and network throughput align with smaller instance constraints. The system achieves 51.88 GB/sec read and 34.76 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB blocks, but registers a PassMark memory score of 1813.3 in the bottom 25%. In application-level benchmarks, the instance delivers 7.31 million Redis SET operations per second and handles small 135M-parameter LLM inference at 822.76 prompt tokens per second and 231.87 text generation tokens per second. Static web serving throughput settles at 5.52 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the F2als_v7 is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and complete absence of local disk, requiring remote storage solutions for stateful operations. However, high CPU clock speeds provide cost-effective dedicated compute capacity. It is best suited for entry-level compute-bound workloads, single-threaded processing pipelines, lightweight batch processing, and microservices requiring high CPU clock rates without significant memory demands.
description: Microsoft Azure F2als_v7 is a compute-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, featuring an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It offers 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) on the x86_64 architecture, 4.0 GB of total RAM (2.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512 and SHA-NI. The instance contains no bundled local storage, no GPUs, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Benchmark testing highlights top-tier single-core performance, achieving 3791.79 in single-core stress-ng and top-tier single-threaded compression speeds, though overall throughput is constrained by the two-core boundary. Because memory capacity is limited to 4.0 GB and local storage is absent, the F2als_v7 provides a cost-efficient profile targeted at single-threaded batch tasks, lightweight microservices, and compute-focused utilities with low memory footprints.
